## Motivation

`parse_arguments("1,000", "number")` currently accepts Python's implicit tuple `(1, 0)`. A GLM-4 tool call then exposes `{"n": [1, 0]}` rather than retaining the original argument text.

Fixes #43147.

## Modifications

Convert tuple results to lists for explicit array schemas. For numeric or untyped arguments, reject tuple results and continue through the existing string fallback. Add regressions for comma expressions, tuple literals, and the serialized GLM-4 tool-call arguments.

## Accuracy Tests

`python test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py` — all 253 tests passed. The original numeric regressions fail on unmodified `main`. The added array regressions fail at the prior PR head and pass with the schema-specific fix.

This is CPU parser validation; model inference was not required for the argument-serialization behavior.

All repository Python, text, configuration, and test-registration pre-commit hooks passed. Unrelated C++ and Rust formatting/Clippy hooks were not run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No model-forward, scheduling, or kernel changes. No inference benchmark was run.

nodes.body:
Thanks for picking this up! One small behaviour note: before this change, an array-typed argument written with a bare comma (e.g. `<arg_value>1, 2</arg_value>` for `{"type": "array"}`) came out as `[1, 2]`, since `json.dumps` turned the tuple into a list. With the tuple rejected unconditionally it now becomes the string `"1, 2"`. Keeping the list when `arg_type == "array"` would avoid that:

```python
if not isinstance(parsed_value, tuple):
    return parsed_value, True
if arg_type == "array":
    return list(parsed_value), True
```

FYI, `glm47_moe_detector.py` (GLM-4.7/5) has its own copy of `parse_arguments` with the same bug. I've opened #43270 for that file only, so the two PRs don't overlap.
Thanks, 288f5b0 looks good to me: array-typed args keep the list and everything else keeps the text, which matches #43270 for GLM-4.7/5, so both parsers now behave the same.

+class TestGlm4ArgumentFallback(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_comma_expressions_remain_strings(self):
+        """Comma expressions must not become arrays without an array schema."""
+        for raw in ("1,000", '"a","b"', "1,", "(1, 2)"):
+            for arg_type in (None, "number"):
+                with self.subTest(raw=raw, arg_type=arg_type):
+                    self.assertEqual(parse_arguments(raw, arg_type), (raw, True))
+
+    def test_array_comma_expressions_remain_arrays(self):
+        """Array schemas preserve comma-separated values as JSON arrays."""
+        for raw, expected in (
+            ("1, 2", [1, 2]),
+            ('"a","b"', ["a", "b"]),
+            ("1,", [1]),
+            ("(1, 2)", [1, 2]),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(raw=raw):
+                self.assertEqual(parse_arguments(raw, "array"), (expected, True))
+
+    def test_tool_call_preserves_comma_value(self):
+        """Tool calls preserve comma values according to their argument schema."""
+        for arg_type, raw, expected in (
+            ("number", "1,000", "1,000"),
+            ("array", "1, 2", [1, 2]),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(arg_type=arg_type):
+                self._assert_tool_call_comma_value(arg_type, raw, expected)
+
+    def _assert_tool_call_comma_value(self, arg_type, raw, expected):
+        tools = [
+            Tool(
+                type="function",
+                function=Function(
+                    name="book",
+                    parameters={
+                        "type": "object",
+                        "properties": {"n": {"type": arg_type}},
+                    },
+                ),
+            )
+        ]
+        text = (
+            "<tool_call>book\n<arg_key>n</arg_key>\n"
+            f"<arg_value>{raw}</arg_value>\n</tool_call>"
+        )
+        calls = Glm4MoeDetector().detect_and_parse(text, tools).calls
+        self.assertEqual(len(calls), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(calls[0].name, "book")
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(calls[0].parameters), {"n": expected})
+
